brief: The school library at night, moonlight through a window: a small blue-black spirit with ink-stained wisps writing in the air with a reed pen, faint glowing lines of verse trailing behind it; you, Dādī and Śuka peering round a shelf; the tree of names glowing softly in a corner.

Dādī on the floor mat of the Ācārya's lamplit house drawing a family tree in her cloth-bound notebook with a reed pen, a trunk with many named branches; you leaning over her shoulder; the slim golden spirit's lamp glowing brighter as each name is read; Śuka on the shelf.
The small grey-blue spirit arranging word-cards into three sentences on the ghat steps, shaking his head at one wrong one that Śuka placed; Dādī watching with arms folded and a smile.

Three groups of readers on the ghat steps: one boy reading alone, two girls sharing a palm leaf, and a row of children reading aloud together; the small grey-blue spirit leaning in with a hand cupped to his ear.
